note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a IRQ 6(I)(c); A06b IRQ 6(I)(c); L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Iraqi Nationality Law No. (26) of 2006, Official Gazette of Iraq Issue No. (4019), 07/03/2006, in the Ministry of Justice's English translation (moj.gov.iq). Every figure the file holds now rests on it, and the dataset is no longer cited. The Ministry of Justice's English translation, laid out as the Gazette, was read; the Arabic Gazette text itself wasn't.

sources.title: Iraqi Nationality Law No. (26) of 2006, Official Gazette of Iraq Issue No. (4019), 07/03/2006, in the Ministry of Justice's English translation (moj.gov.iq)
sources.said: Article 3: It shall be considered an Iraqi national: a. Whoever born to an Iraqi father or an Iraqi mother. b. Whoever was born in Iraq to unknown parents ... Article 5: The Minister may be considered an Iraqi national who was born in Iraq and reached the age of adulthood therein from a non-Iraqi father who was also born in it and was a habitual resident at the birth of his/ her child, provided that the child submits a request ... Article 6: First: The Minister may accept the naturalization of a non-Iraqi when the following conditions are met: ... c. He/ she should reside in Iraq legally for a period of not less than ten consecutive years prior to submitting the application. ... Article 10: First: An Iraqi person who obtains a foreign nationality shall retain his/ her Iraqi nationality, unless he/ she declares in writing renouncing his/ her Iraqi nationality.

atBirth.descentAbroad: Person is born abroad to a male citizen.; The Minister may consider Iraqi any person born outside Iraq to an Iraqi mother and an unknown or stateless father, if he chooses the Iraqi nationality, within one year from coming of age (reaching the age of majority), unless he fails to do so, due to difficult circumstances, provided that he is residing within Iraq at the time of application for the Iraqi nationality.
